# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary – 2026-08-06

The top tier—Nasdaq 100 and NYSE—dominate decisively, combining ultra-low ILLIQ scores (0.0024% and 0.0058% per $1M traded respectively) with substantial comparable volumes ($312.4M and $169.9M). A clear second tier comprises Tokyo, Euronext, and Hong Kong, where ILLIQ ranges from 0.0282% to 0.0351% per $1M traded and turnover ratios span 0.42% to 2.73%. Tokyo notably exhibits the highest turnover ratio (2.7274%) despite modest comparable volume ($47.5M), suggesting concentrated activity among tracked constituents. The mid-pack—SIX Swiss, Korea, LSE, and Xetra—reveals important metric divergence: Korea Exchange shows the weakest ILLIQ reading (0.1690% per $1M traded) alongside the widest AR spread (1.5006%), yet maintains respectable turnover (0.7452%), indicating volatile execution costs despite reasonable order flow. Conversely, Xetra and SIX Swiss post tighter spreads (0.5940% and 0.5694% respectively) than their ILLIQ scores would suggest, signaling intermittent large-trade friction. London Stock Exchange trails at rank 8 with 0.0783% per $1M ILLIQ and 0.7794% spread. Overall, geographic consolidation in North America remains pronounced.
